It is one indicator of the trade-off between timeliness and accuracy, and also captures methodological improvements that come through our annual Blue Books.

The main methodological and data improvements in Blue Book 2026 are the incorporation of the Annual Survey of Goods and Services (ASGS), which gives us more information on products that are produced by the services industries, and changes to our estimates of actual and imputed rentals. We maintain a transparent approach in showing revisions to UK gross domestic product (GDP) estimates by publishing real-time estimates of GDP, alongside our data vintages, and by providing a timely assessment of these revisions.

There is a mean revision between the first estimate and the final estimate of positive 0.1 percentage points over the period Quarter 1 (Jan to Mar) 1961 to Quarter 4 (Oct to Dec) 2023; for the period Quarter 1 2020 to Quarter 4 2023, there is a mean revision of positive 0.3 percentage points, which includes the impact of the uncertainty around the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

When we look at the sign of quarterly GDP growth, of the 175 times where the growth in the first estimate was positive, 168 of these (96%) have remained positive in the final estimate, while 42 of the 64 (66%) instances where the growth in the first estimate was negative have remained negative.
